baseline.libgphoto2_ref: ian-morgan99/libgphoto2 main. ADVANCED from v97's pin 3fb26e536ac169e4970d69516a9d45daf62563f5, because driver main had moved past that commit while work accumulated unreleased on feature/astro-native-platesolve -- the tree was building from a driver commit no release had ever named. The delta is exactly one commit and it is documentation only: `git log --oneline 3fb26e536..7e6dec95f` returns a single line (docs: state which repo owns which work) and touches no camlib or library source. scripts/pin-divergence-check.sh reports ancestry OK, patch-equiv 0 genuinely missing, PASS. So the shipped .so set is expected to match v97 byte for byte and should be verified against v97's install-manifest.json. Carries #233 capability row and #235 K-1 II shutter gate from PR #144, the deferred-Bulb cancellation fix from PR #139, and the K-3 III Bulb shutter-list synthesis (#241).
baseline.patcher_ref: feature/astro-native-platesolve at the cut commit 42eedb0dc, 53 commits ahead of bf1aad4c1067338b859643b264e7d5cda2b213b9 (the tree astro-v97 was built from). The published manifest recomputes this from git at build time; the value here is the commit this summary was written against.
baseline.why_this_is_a_cut_and_not_another_increm: Work after v97 accumulated on feature/astro-native-platesolve without being called a release, so 53 patcher commits and one driver commit sat unnamed and the driver pin drifted behind main unnoticed. This candidate names them: it is the formal cut for that accumulated work, with the pin advanced to current driver main and PREVIOUS_LIB_BASELINE set to v97's pin so the superset gate compares against the release that actually shipped and ran on hardware, rather than against v94.

purpose: Formally cut the work that accumulated after astro-v97 without being released: ship the station-mode Wi-Fi kit as its own SD-rooted archive alongside polaris-astro.zip, carry forward the web UI changes that stop it claiming a camera write succeeded when the head actually rejected it, and re-pin the driver to current libgphoto2 main so provenance names commits that exist on a branch a third party can fetch.

changes.summary: The astro bundle build now cross-builds libnl, iw and wpa_supplicant and ships them as polaris-wifi.zip, rooted at polaris-wifi/ so it unzips at the card root. The boot hook starts auto-join only when /app/sd/polaris-wifi/autojoin exists and polaris-autojoin.sh is executable, so the build fails closed if either the kit or that script is missing rather than installing silently nothing. setup-wifi.sh writes a PSK hash with mode 600, never puts the passphrase on a command line where ps would show it, and strips the plaintext copy wpa_passphrase emits as a comment.

Copyleft notices now travel inside polaris-wifi.zip rather than only in the bundle's licenses/ directory, which sits outside COPY-TO-SD-CARD-ROOT and therefore never reaches a user who copies just that archive. libnl is LGPL-2.1 and is linked statically into all four wifi binaries, so section 4 requires the offer to accompany them. LICENCE-wifi.txt names the exact versions built and their upstream URLs, derived from the tarball filenames actually present so the text cannot drift from the artifacts beside it.

The Astro web UI reconciles camera writes instead of assuming they landed. The head answers ok:true and then reports the truth in a trailing ret: field, so a write the camera dropped is now retried and reported as not applied rather than painted with the value the user chose. Also: acting endpoints no longer fire on GET, and the connected camera's name is shown over the live frame.
install_astro.sh refreshes an already-installed boot hook when the payload updates, so a re-release takes effect instead of the SD copy being ignored because /app/astro/polaris-httpd already existed.

scripts/resolve-release-inputs.sh resolves the stock FwPkt and a clean libgphoto2 main, and refuses to choose between two usable trees rather than picking one silently. The release skill now makes it the first step, because several sessions asserted the stock firmware was absent when it had been on disk the whole time.

known_limits: Exposure compensation (267) still fails on the K-1 II. Reproduced 2026-11-07 against the v97 camera stack verified by binary hash: no reply at all, pending never cleared, badge sequence EV: applying x24 then EV: not applied x6, while ISO, white balance and aperture round-trip in the same sequence on the same body. Tracked as #233; this candidate does not fix it.

The -2110 write-rejection rate is unmeasured on any current build. The only figure on record (62 percent of K-1 II exposure writes, from commit f593d91) exists solely in a commit message with no retained log, and the 2026-11-07 run could not see it because that harness reads back through /api/exposure rather than parsing ret:. Filed as #274.

Wi-Fi auto-join has never been qualified on a live network. The mount's own access point powers its radio down roughly 60 seconds after the last client disconnects, which blocked the join attempt during development; the kit is built, deployed to an SD card and unit-checked, but a successful association to a real router is not proven by this candidate.

The dashboard's join-at-power-up checkbox does nothing: it posts a parameter the server does not accept, so it silently reverts. Tracked as #273. Use setup-wifi.sh, polaris-apsta.sh up and touch autojoin instead.
Built without astrometry indexes. They are a one-time copy and do not change between releases, so they are deliberately kept out of the per-release archive.
Candidate build only. Nothing here is installed, staged, flashed, rebooted or uploaded, and no camera was attached during this build.
validation_focus: Unzip polaris-astro.zip and polaris-wifi.zip at the SD card root, not into a subfolder, then reboot and confirm polaris-httpd listens on :8090.

Wi-Fi: run setup-wifi.sh, then polaris-apsta.sh up, confirm an address and reachability, then touch /app/sd/polaris-wifi/autojoin and reboot to confirm the join happens at power-up. Wake the mount first, because its access point radio sleeps after the last client leaves.
Confirm wpa.conf contains no plaintext passphrase: grep -c '#psk=' must be 0, and the file must be mode 600.

K-1 II: re-run the exposure write/read-back/restore sequence for shutter, aperture, ISO, white balance and EV. Expect shutter to report a refusal honestly rather than painting a stale value; EV is still expected to fail (#233).
Confirm the camera payload is unchanged from v97 by comparing ptp2.so, pentax.so and libgphoto2.so.6 against v97's install-manifest.json.
